label: copy-phase input t fed back at the first or second copy step
explanation: Fires when the token t is the input during the first copy-phase steps: recall_idx 1, where the input is orig(0)=t, and recall_idx 2, where the input is orig(1)=t. Magnitude depends on position. At recall_idx 1 (first original token is t) it is near max (about 0.8-1.0 of max) and holds about 79% of activation mass. At recall_idx 2 it is much weaker (about 0.1-0.4 of max, about 21% of mass). At recall_idx 3 it only gives faint traces (about 0.02). Later copy steps with input t give nothing, and neither do t inputs in the original phase, the delimiter, or any other token. The output token, L and next_out barely matter. The small number of false positives are mostly short sequences (L=3-4) where t is the second token.

issues: The claims check out. On the test split, the predicate scores precision 0.975, recall 0.978, F1 0.976 and mass recall 0.999. Outside the copy phase it catches 0.08% of active steps and holds 0.004% of activation mass. In the dev profile, in_tok == t holds 100% of the mass, recall_idx 1 holds 79.3% and recall_idx 2 holds 20.5%. recall_idx 3 shows only faint traces (704 active steps, 0.1% of mass), and nothing fires at recall_idx 4 or later.
recall_idx == 1 with input t has precision 1.0 on test (16774 predicted steps).

The false positives form a real but small pattern, and the explanation already says they come from short sequences. At recall_idx 2 with input t, precision is 0.15 for L=3 (438 steps) and 0.81 for L=4 (2481 steps). It is 1.0 for L=5, L=6 and L=9. In the L=4 false positives, t is orig(1) and the step is 6, so the feature seems to be suppressed when few copy steps remain (small to_go).
The missed activations (745 on test, 0.1% of mass) are the faint recall_idx 3 activations of about 0.01-0.05, so they are minor and expected.
